authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: Previously reviewed comparative evidence: CDIAL 6328 dina lists Prakrit diṇa and Nepali, Assamese, Bengali, Maithili, Awadhi and Hindi din “day”. It explicitly warns that Punjabi/Western Pahari din is borrowed from Hindi or Sanskrit, as are potentially Gujarati/Marathi forms; those transmission-sensitive matches are held. Updated disposition under the user’s explicit cross-Indo-Aryan policy: link this supported etymon despite unresolved inheritance versus intra-Indo-Aryan borrowing. The reflex edge records etymological family affiliation provisionally; it does not establish uninterrupted inheritance or an immediate donor. Prior hold: CDIAL 6328 marks several western din forms as Hindi/Sanskrit loans; establish the immediate local transmission before using a reflex edge.

proposals.evidence: Previously reviewed comparative evidence: CDIAL 142 accha gives Punjabi acchā “good”, explicitly borrowed into standard Hindi, and Old Marwari āchyo/āchī. The route is decided locally: standard Hindi is linked to the existing Punjabi attestation; direct western āch- continuations are kept separate from unresolved regional contact forms. Updated disposition under the user’s explicit cross-Indo-Aryan policy: link this supported etymon despite unresolved inheritance versus intra-Indo-Aryan borrowing. The reflex edge records etymological family affiliation provisionally; it does not establish uninterrupted inheritance or an immediate donor. Prior hold: CDIAL 142 distinguishes inherited western āch- forms from Punjabi > Hindi acchā; the survey lect’s immediate borrowing route is not established.
